verdict.tagline: Mass battles shine, but early hurdles and deep progression drag.
for_you_if: you enjoy large-scale medieval tactical combat
you are willing to master complex directional blocking
you want epic sandbox kingdom management
not_for_you_if: you experience crashes during tutorial loading screens
you expect a polished and stable campaign experience
you are frustrated by repetitive early quests

distortion_flags.sentence: Player sentiment rises sharply past the initial hours before dipping slightly among long-term players.
Recent reviews score lower compared to the lifetime average.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players encounter severe bugs in the opening tutorial, broken mods, and technical instability during loading screens.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience crashes during the tutorial and loading screens.

citations.review_text: Everything was going smoothly, then it crashed, when I left the training grounds. It just kept crashing, every time I tried to load. I was able to load an earlier save, but it crashed at the same spot. I tried to implement some fixes, but the time limit for a return was almost up, so I just ended up returning it. It did seem like an interesting game, but unfortunately, I wasn't able to play it.

I will change my rating when the game no longer need mods for bug fixes and to not feel just like a soulless battle simulator.  Notice how most positive reviews are with the game being modded in some way.  They add an expensive DLC which just adds more bugs and broken mechanics rather than fixing bugs/crashes in the base game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the opening tutorial is difficult or impossible to complete because objectives like recruiting soldiers or finding the village head are bugged or hard to navigate.

citations.review_text:
👎 After this tutorial, I have no desire to play this game anymore.

I spent more than an hour trying to complete the tutorial at the very beginning of the game. The objective was to recruit soldiers from a village, but the village had zero recruits available. Because of that, the tutorial became completely stuck. I couldn’t continue the quest, couldn’t buy supplies, and couldn’t properly interact with other settlements because the game kept forcing me to complete an objective that was literally impossible.

I wasted over an hour trying to figure out whether I was doing something wrong. I reloaded saves, traveled around the map, and searched for solutions, but nothing worked.

To make this even more frustrating, I didn’t just buy the base game. I bought the complete edition with every available add-on and content pack, paying around $60 in total, and I still can’t properly play this supposedly amazing game because the opening tutorial is broken.

This is one of the worst first impressions I’ve ever had in a game. If a new player can get completely soft-locked by a bug within the first few minutes, that is a serious failure in both game design and quality assurance.

As a result, I have completely lost the desire to play. I’m uninstalling the game. My sincere congratulations to the developers and everyone responsible for allowing this bug to remain in the very beginning of the game. Truly an excellent introduction.

Bannerlord looked like a game I could have spent hundreds of hours playing, but my experience ended before it even properly began. We will never meet again.

I think I played it before and abandoned. Tried it now and couldn't progress through first quest... spent 10 minutes wandering around that village and wasn't able to find the head of the village..... that's dumb

The first game was great. Then they must have switched producers because the tutorial is complete ass. The field combat is substantially worse.

-10 / 10 would not even force my worst enemies to play this game. That should qualify as a crime against humanity.

I couldn't get past the tutorial before I asked for a refund. Incredibly confusing UI. There are a bunch of white arrows that blink around on the screen like they are supposed to tell you where to go but I couldn't make any sense of it. The game is heavy heavy into the role play aspect even such that when you are creating a character you can't just allocate points to a stat you have to pick a backstory and you get to select from choices of point allocations based on the storyline you chose (like are you a blacksmith, did you like to brawl when you were a kid..) The game looks like it was from the 90s the way the graphics and the gameplay felt but I gave it a chance through all that. The killer for me was not being able to complete the tutorial cause I got to a town and was supposed to find someone and searched everywhere and couldn't figure out the UI so I was like nah not my game
One of the worse tutorials ever in any game I have played. I gave up and uninstalled.

citations.review_text: from the tutorial I already got that the hit register in this game is hit or miss on horse back and the bow feels clunky and akward.

Perhaps buy it on sale, I only played for 30 minutes but it plays exactly like warband. It's pretty much a copy and paste and there wasn't really a reason to continue playing. Combat and horse riding is ass. Villages and missions play the same. The beginning dealing with bandits is the same. Map UI sucks and the perks system makes no sense.

I kinda still do love this game and like to play it but the main issue for me is that its way too expensive for an unfinished game but it has SO MUCH potential and thats so frustrating it could be top 5 games of this type if just some thought was put into making it better and adding new stuff. Among other things i dislike the ranged weapon leveling just useing them is so funky dont even get me speaking about spears omg

claims.claim: Reviewers state that mod support is unstable and game updates break existing mods.

citations.review_text:
I do not recommend this game until the mod support is stable as of now if you take a list of 100 mods only 5 of them will be compatible. The game has a great foundation for modding but the stability of the mods is beyond egregious for the time that this game has come out. This is an L for the devs NOT the modders. Its borderline disrespectful from the devs to their modders and community due to the fact that the base game is basic and doesnt add much more content over any other mount and blade game. Until the required mod support is added between updates it will be a no recommended from me.

Edit: Bannerlord v1.4.7 DOES NOT ADD ENOUGH CONTENT TO REQUIRE UPDATING MODS THIS IS A MOD SUPPORT ISSUE FROM THE DEVS
Modding in this game is a plague.

None of the mods work without some serious fiddling. Congratulations, you made the most moddable game's sequel into TRASH. Also the BASE game is just a facelift and literally the very same game as the one from 25 years ago.

what made bannerlord strong - you guys destroy, I just hope modders will keep up with your sudden ground breaking updates, because it seems that biggest mods - that half of the mods library were dependent on, have been abandonded. I bought this game just to play it modded but i was met with a very sorry state of things. The worst of it is that this problem isnt even addressed by creators studio but they keep updating it with "minor bugfixes updates" which for whatever reason  need 4GB download and just worsen modding scene

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the combat system requires memorizing directional attack and block indicators, which some find overly complicated while others recommend practicing high mouse sensitivity to master.

citations.review_text:
I absolutely love Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord. This to me, hands down is the best game I have EVER played. So much content, best fun. Absolute gem of a game, seriously, play this and get hooked on it for life for this game, it never get's old.

You have Steam Workshop mods as well if you are into having mods and lots of great ones too. As for the game, it's a mixture of multiple games, Age Of Empires, Rome Total War, Risk, even Skyrim etc. I cannot believe that this game has not at current, it doesn't have overwhelmingly positive reviews, now that is insane, how could a game this good not be overwhelmingly positive!? Seriously, get this and you won't be disappointed, man, best game ever. Now, my only gripe is the combat and commands...

Now this can be quite complicated, as you attack, block and so forth, there are these arrow icons which means, that is the direction of where you are going to strike your enemy or block in. A great tip on keyboard and mouse, high mouse sesitivity, fast moving for good reflexes, move the mouse like crazy to kill opponents like a mad thing, study each attack and know how to parry it. There are custom battles, do 1v1 on AI or go in sandbox, go in an area and practise fighting, you will die again and again but don't worry, once you get the hang of it, you'll always be playing this game lol. 2 thumbs up from me, highly recommend. Look up guides if you are unsure though.

If you are concerned about the amount of violence in Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord, you can toggle blood on and off in gameplay settings at anytime.

If your looking for a continuation of the previous game with this is not that, they basically stripped away everything that made the original good and basically turned it into slop. The combat is incredibly annoying gone are the days of being able to win duels against enemies easily now you need to now memorize the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MB Napoleonic Wars esc combat system meaning you can't just block hits anymore with long weapons you need to actually focus on the enemies attacks then reblock them meaning the skill floor is basically at bed rock and the skill ceiling is the beat saber spam swinging block buttons in hopes to hit a enemy back. Remember when you could win fights in 1-2 swings in the arena well now enemies can take up to 4 hits depending on where you hit them. The economy system is also super buggy, I tried playing as a merchant and although I could make money sometimes prices would just seemingly randomly drop meaning I lost or just barely broke even.

Remember in warband when the arena sucked ass but atleast it was fun because even though you were basically 1v20 with random weapons you were equally matched and enemies spawned in over time, yeah well im happy to report that arena sucks even more ass now since you on top of having to learn the new combat system still get ganged up on.

I had fun for a while doing trading, random quests and other things for about 2 hours before I got ambushed by a entire bandit calvary company, lost all my men and rage quit since I'd basically been playing 2 hours at that point and I didn't have a save. I don't know how they did it but they some how made Warband's UI better then Bannerlord, a game that is 16 years old has better UI then this 40 dollar slop fest. I mean holy ♥♥♥♥ 6 years since early access and 4 years since launch and this game is still priced at 40 bucks. And they released DLCs which I'm gonna be honest should of just been a update if the game was going to stay at 40 bucks. Considering you can buy Warband for half th…

The game is just a boring, miserable grind once the novelty wears off.

It took about a dozen hours to get enough renown to become a vassal (the back few of which was a grind of raiding enemy caravans for money and fame as a merc), and in this time I'd managed to build a 100 strong semi-elite party, had about 30k in the bank and owned a brewery. Within days I was bankrupt, because the overall upkeep on my party, my garrison and it's militia was over 2000 a day, my brewery averages around 200 (15 grand wasted I guess) and settlements income around 250.

Then within a month, it was taken from me by enemies because no allies would help.

Either I'm missing something, or the game punishes you for finally reaching any part of the game that isn't just grinding boring, easy battles.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the inclusion of physics-based combat involving large-scale unit battles.

citations.review_text: Tons of fun, sandboxy map fun combined with excellent 500 v 500 physics based combat.

A large world with international politics and living settlements.  You begin living on the fringes of society and must build a gang of hoodlums into a private army.  The game permits a wide range of routes to do this.   The key decision in the game is how to build that army.  What mix of infantry, archers, cavalry from what culture.  It is possible for the game to simulate battles but battles are this game's specialty.  Suprisingly intuitive field commands.  A virtuoso blend of tactics and strategy.  Highly recommended.  8/10.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the early game progression involves hunting bandits and participating in repetitive quests.

citations.review_text: I expected to become the greatest military ruler and build a massive army but instead im hunting bandits and struggling to own one settlement. A+

The idea behind the game is great, and it feels strong at first but it becomes clear that it is still unfinished, unevenly developed, and stretched too thin, still 6 years after early access release.

Each sandbox playthrough starts with a heavy amount of grinding before the game properly opens up. Early progression relies on a very limited set of repetitive quests and constant small-scale fights against bandits. These encounters offer minimal rewards, often barely covering losses. For example, defeating a bandit group might yield a couple hundred gold and some low-value loot, while losing a single troop or piece of equipment can cost just as much or more. For perspective a war horse for one single soldier usually costs around 1,000 gold.

Progression from a new character to a functional mercenary or vassal leader requires an excessive amount of grinding. Even activities like tournaments quickly become repetitive and are required in large numbers to reach the first clan tier, which would get you a semi decent war band.

Some systems like stealth, smithing, and the war sails naval dlc could have been added later after fixing the core issues. Instead of strengthening the foundation they add additional layers on top of systems that already feel underdeveloped. Politics, diplomacy, managing AI armies are very weak areas of the game. 

Mods are often suggested as a fix but in practice they don't fully resolve the underlying issues. There are too many interconnected systems needing adjustment, and setting up a stable modded experience can itself be time-consuming, inconsistent, frustrating, and at the end a bit of a waste of time.

The game ultimately contains a lot of shallow systems that lose depth quickly. The potential is definitely there, especially in combat, sieges, tournaments, but it needs bug fixing, balancing, diplomacy. If the foundation were more polished and focused, the game could be outstanding and expansions like stealth, smithing, or naval combat could b…

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the artificial intelligence governing kingdom politics and faction decisions distributes captured properties to lords with nearby small holdings rather than the player clan.

citations.review_text:
the AI is absolutely abysmal. Of course if you're looking for any improvements to battleAI as well as their decision-making, you'll be inundated with mods that hook the NPC's up to some actual AI API. 
It couldn't be more of a braindead take to think that's what this game needed.
You'd think the devs would try to fix this game as it is nowhere near finished or acceptable to pay for the game in the state that it's in. Maybe overhaul progression, the main campaign, since it's got severe scaling issues?

At some point once you do some quests, you get the ability to assemble an item that's supposed to represent your authority on Calradia. Yet the internet suggests giving it to your enemy instead, as the entire map will zerg rush them instead, making you the de-facto winner of most engagements despite the fact that you gave the wonder-item away. I mean, who the ♥♥♥♥ thought of this? Cool game, an improvement over Warband, but not at all what's chalked up to be. Don't be fooled by the YouTube videos. Functionally, the game is in a sorry state. Get it on a massive sale, no full price, and enjoy it that way.

Joining armies is absolutely terrible as well, just as an addendum. Going from mercenary to fief owner is a genuine joke as your army leader will roam the map like an idiot, sieging useless objectives, and walking by city capitals, disengaging sieges on a whim, and softlocking itself. One of the most awe inducing examples of this is the AI army meeting a bigger enemy army and constantly running back into a friendly castle. When the enemy army tries to back out, the AI army leader will exit the castle since the enemy is outside of their immediate eyesight, causing the enemy army to scatter back into a chase, as the AI leader will then again retreat back to the same castle. Months, years can pass like this in-game, sucking you dry of food & wages. Total ass.

I like this game. I suggest it. I just want to talk about what I dislike so it can hopefully, maybe, if I'm super lucky, might get fixed.


AI gets huge advantages like greater siege equipment accuracy, summoning massive armies out of nowhere, and the ability to completely lock you out of getting new property unless you have max level trading. The player cannot obtain any of these benefits and it's extremely annoying. The "being locked out of property" is especially demeaning and removes the point of playing the game from entire playstyles for long periods of time.

The AI locks you out of getting new property if you choose to be apart of a kingdom instead of starting your own. Essentially, even if you're the most powerful and useful clan in the kingdom, and capture a city, the AI will prioritize giving it to NPC leaders with like one castle, or leaders with nearby property. If they're broke as hell, and have a single, run-down castle happens to be slightly close to the property in question, they'll get like 70% council support by default, normally 90-100%, which is too high to fight with influence. God forbid you help your country and push further, because they'll keep giving it to the broke loser. So you have to save-scum, or buy it with the max level trading skill.

Incredibly frustrating game, that lacks depth and quality of game mechanics.

This game has one and only one good component, which is large scale battles. Everything else is more or less lacking. 

Governing system is dumb. You are saying that I have to run around the world to find a companion of right culture, otherwise I get penalty? Oh, don't forget that percentage of those wanderers is diminishing among the ones I find, maybe 20 %. Too bad. I can command 2000 men armies, but can't find a one guy to run a castle? Make it make sense.

Workshops or trading? Boring. Buy, sell, forget, no depth.

Marriage and clan management? Nothing special here.

What really buggers me about this game is that it lacks a strategic and middle-management layer. In the start player is the small guy and does things "hands on" by himself. You have the control. Later on player becomes this big war lord that just commands armies and does not bother with small details anymore. HOWEVER, you are still expected to do many things yourself.

Need a troops from your garrison? Why can't I send a messenger and have someone bring them to me and my army? No, redirect your thousand man army to the other side of the world to go there yourself. Repeat as many times as you have garrisons and there, you just lost couple of cities.

This game really needs more control on middle-management and player should be able to do things as a general would: by giving commands for others to take care of.

This game lacks any strategic planning. Why I can't gather with my fellow vassal lords and say: "I will take that castle after I conquer it, aight?". Hell no, you do all the work and others get the benefits, randomly of course.

I mean, who the ♥♥♥♥ thought of this? Cool game, an improvement over Warband, but not at all what's chalked up to be. Don't be fooled by the YouTube videos. Functionally, the game is in a sorry state. Get it on a massive sale, no full price, and enjoy it that way.

Joining armies is absolutely terrible as well, just as an addendum. Going from mercenary to fief owner is a genuine joke as your army leader will roam the map like an idiot, sieging useless objectives, and walking by city capitals, disengaging sieges on a whim, and softlocking itself. One of the most awe inducing examples of this is the AI army meeting a bigger enemy army and constantly running back into a friendly castle. When the enemy army tries to back out, the AI army leader will exit the castle since the enemy is outside of their immediate eyesight, causing the enemy army to scatter back into a chase, as the AI leader will then again retreat back to the same castle. Months, years can pass like this in-game, sucking you dry of food & wages. Total ass.

I like this game. I suggest it. I just want to talk about what I dislike so it can hopefully, maybe, if I'm super lucky, might get fixed.


AI gets huge advantages like greater siege equipment accuracy, summoning massive armies out of nowhere, and the ability to completely lock you out of getting new property unless you have max level trading. The player cannot obtain any of these benefits and it's extremely annoying. The "being locked out of property" is especially demeaning and removes the point of playing the game from entire playstyles for long periods of time.

The AI locks you out of getting new property if you choose to be apart of a kingdom instead of starting your own. Essentially, even if you're the most powerful and useful clan in the kingdom, and capture a city, the AI will prioritize giving it to NPC leaders with like one castle, or leaders with nearby property. If they're broke as hell, and have a single, run-down castle happens to be slightly close to the property in question, they'll get like 70% council support by default, normally 90-100%, which is too high to fight with influence. God forbid you help your country and push further, because they'll keep giving it to the broke loser. So you have to save-scum, or buy it with the max level trading skill.

Incredibly frustrating game, that lacks depth and quality of game mechanics.

This game has one and only one good component, which is large scale battles. Everything else is more or less lacking. 

Governing system is dumb. You are saying that I have to run around the world to find a companion of right culture, otherwise I get penalty? Oh, don't forget that percentage of those wanderers is diminishing among the ones I find, maybe 20 %. Too bad. I can command 2000 men armies, but can't find a one guy to run a castle? Make it make sense.

Workshops or trading? Boring. Buy, sell, forget, no depth.

Marriage and clan management? Nothing special here.

What really buggers me about this game is that it lacks a strategic and middle-management layer. In the start player is the small guy and does things "hands on" by himself. You have the control. Later on player becomes this big war lord that just commands armies and does not bother with small details anymore. HOWEVER, you are still expected to do many things yourself.

Need a troops from your garrison? Why can't I send a messenger and have someone bring them to me and my army? No, redirect your thousand man army to the other side of the world to go there yourself. Repeat as many times as you have garrisons and there, you just lost couple of cities.

This game really needs more control on middle-management and player should be able to do things as a general would: by giving commands for others to take care of.

This game lacks any strategic planning. Why I can't gather with my fellow vassal lords and say: "I will take that castle after I conquer it, aight?". Hell no, you do all the work and others get the benefits, randomly of course.

My ally AI lords and kings really ruin this game for me. They don't do their part, but rather they do everything that harms the greater benefit of the kingdom. What, someone is asking for a peace while we have three simultaneous wars? How dare you! Let's do nothing and get w…

The idea behind the game is great, and it feels strong at first but it becomes clear that it is still unfinished, unevenly developed, and stretched too thin, still 6 years after early access release.

Each sandbox playthrough starts with a heavy amount of grinding before the game properly opens up. Early progression relies on a very limited set of repetitive quests and constant small-scale fights against bandits. These encounters offer minimal rewards, often barely covering losses. For example, defeating a bandit group might yield a couple hundred gold and some low-value loot, while losing a single troop or piece of equipment can cost just as much or more. For perspective a war horse for one single soldier usually costs around 1,000 gold.

Progression from a new character to a functional mercenary or vassal leader requires an excessive amount of grinding. Even activities like tournaments quickly become repetitive and are required in large numbers to reach the first clan tier, which would get you a semi decent war band.

Some systems like stealth, smithing, and the war sails naval dlc could have been added later after fixing the core issues. Instead of strengthening the foundation they add additional layers on top of systems that already feel underdeveloped. Politics, diplomacy, managing AI armies are very weak areas of the game. 

Mods are often suggested as a fix but in practice they don't fully resolve the underlying issues. There are too many interconnected systems needing adjustment, and setting up a stable modded experience can itself be time-consuming, inconsistent, frustrating, and at the end a bit of a waste of time.

The game ultimately contains a lot of shallow systems that lose depth quickly. The potential is definitely there, especially in combat, sieges, tournaments, but it needs bug fixing, balancing, diplomacy. If the foundation were more polished and focused, the game could be outstanding and expansions like stealth, smithing, or naval combat could b…

claims.claim: Companions and other characters lack depth, personality, and distinctive traits due to randomization.

citations.review_text:
I have a love hate relationship with this game... On one hand, it feels like a massive improvement on warband but on the other it somehow feels soulless in comparison. I find it hard to pin down the reason behind this, however I can name a few issues that lead to the feeling of soullessness. 

First off, we'll go to characters. Both companions and members of other clans feel flat and lack any depth or personality. This I feel is compounded by the nature of how the companions are randomised and not fixed personalities and skill sets that make them iconic. This lack of things being iconic definitely stretches to the fixed characters and even extends into the quests (which were just as flat in warband but at least the characters reacted interestingly to your choices).

The aesthetic is one I regularly have conflict with, the styles of armour are sometime beautiful and other times incredibly awful. plenty of armours you'd like to combined don't now we have more detailed meshes and textures than warband and because there's no way to paint armour for example or there's just poor integration of different armour sets put together on character models.

The diplomacy in this game sucks and may as well be made up of four buttons. war, peace but f*ck you pay me money, peace but here's all my money too and white peace. Any of these interactions are often followed by another declaration of war by the faction furthest away because maybe the weather pattern or some sh*t. You can't even make alliances, you can literally be best friends with a faction leader, be married to one of their children and have their grandkids with you  and they will still sprint over to you moments after declaring war from the other hemisphere.

That's just a few of points I can easily identify there's plenty of other small bits that upset me and plenty of good bits like it running fairly well since full release, the arena is fun (could do with a little more variety though), the dynasty element is pretty co…

Listen i been a M&B fan since childhood but as amazing as this game is, the flaws very quickly start to add up. I wish steam had a meh review option.
It's a good game, riddled with flaws that I wouldn't enjoy if i wasn't nostalgia blinded and loving the series to death, i would not reccomend.

Battles and general fighting are good, as a warband fan, i'd say Bannerlord does a huge leap as a upgrade. Visuals are good, especially with the war sails dlc, there are some gorgeous views. I have nothing bad to say about these two, as the only thing of complaint is that the faces start to get repetitive. (But hey I am 421h into the game, i'm no one to complain)

General troop trees are a great, each faction has a basic troop tree, and a elite troop tree. Very fun stuff. The only minor thing of annoyance is that cavalry costs mounts to train up. But given how good Cav is, its not that horrendous late game.

Fiefs have a inate militia, that will always protect the fief. This makes losing fiefs quite hard, and capturing them, the exact same. Its quite good as it makes gaining a castle or a town in a siege quite rewarding.

Companions are a mixed bag, if you like story heavy companions, they are not great. I don't mind as most of them are randomly generated, come with unique set of skills and make for unique playthroughs without having the same companions (Sorry Jeremus, we still love you). This does result in some game starts where a world starts without a companion good at some specific skill. But its rare and can still be trained up.

Stealth system was added post launch, and honestly as barebones as it is, it works. Quite cool.

Trading becomes quite fun especially when you spec into it, and you can ignore half the game just doing trading, and collapsing city economies with overflow of goods, as well as collapsing your satchel with the amount of coins you get. (trust me its not nearly enough for late game anyway). Workshops tend to be quite good, not as good as warband, but …

The base game just feels shallow. The idea behind Bannerlord is great, but the execution never really reaches its potential. A lot of the time it honestly feels more like Warband with better graphics and UI rather than a true next step for the series.

NPCs mostly feel like moving army generators instead of actual characters. There’s barely any meaningful interaction with them, no real personality, and very little reason to care about anyone in the world. Diplomacy is also extremely basic. Kingdoms are basically either at war, neutral, or allied, and you have almost no real influence over any of it. Wars start out of nowhere with a simple vote and there’s no buildup, tension, negotiation, or politics leading up to it. The world ends up feeling static and lifeless because of it.

The AI can also be incredibly dumb. During sieges, ranged troops will happily stand in completely exposed positions getting filled with arrows instead of using cover while reloading or repositioning. Stuff like that happens way too often.

The combat is still the best part of the game though. Big battles are fun, sieges can be chaotic in a good way, and when everything works properly the game can genuinely be addictive.

MODS:
Honestly, the modding community carries this game hard. A huge amount of the depth, quality of life, diplomacy improvements, AI fixes, and general polish comes from mods. The work modders have done is seriously impressive.

The problem is the developers don’t seem to have really considered how dependent the game has become on modding. Almost every update breaks something. Even after you finally get a stable mod list working, another update comes out and suddenly you’re spending hours trying to figure out which mod broke the game this time.

What makes it more frustrating is that a lot of these updates feel minor compared to the damage they do to the modding scene. Sometimes modders already fixed the issue months or years earlier, then the devs finally release their own…

claims.claim: Core campaign activities revolve heavily around an endless grind of global conquest, lacking deep mechanics in secondary features like smithing and town management.

citations.review_text:
I went hard on warband, their earlier game but bannerlord was a terrible disappointment. I played 100hr,  400 personal army size and player made kingdom out of respect for the series but I do NOT enjoy this game enough to seek global conquest.

The gameplay cycle is pretty bad and unrewarding leading the player to auto battle their soul away. NPC AI behavior feels insanely forced and trollsy. Expect to get griefed by the AI decision making, ally or not. Skill tree chokes you into only mastering 2-3 attribute trees per character which is pretty lame. 

Was overall a grind fest that I committed to just to become established and form a kingdom. After that is an infinite treadmill grind for global conquest which will not be an active gameplay experience.

If there was a "only good with mods" option I'd pick that, but there isn't and I can't in good conscience recommend anyone spend money on the vanilla game without that qualifier. 

Excluding the War Sails DLC, the game has barely made any strides since 2020. It's somewhat more stable, but otherwise still feels like an early access game. There are glaring voids where diplomacy, family, troop outfitting, smithing, and just general depth and breadth of various features should be. Conquest is the ONLY thing to do in the vanilla game. Mods can fix all that though, so if you're comfortable spending a couple hours delving through Nexus (not the Workshop) finding the exactly correct versions of the mods you need for the specific version of the game you're running, THEN it's a great game. You just have to make sure to install a specific version of the game. Every time the devs release even the smallest update it breaks the game and every mod.

I would honestly consider giving this a positive review if the devs vowed never to touch the game again, and just let the modders finish it from here.

I played this a lot. I like this game. But I do not recommend this game. I think they've done a very good job with the battle mechanics, which are just kind of a fun grind to veg out on. The battles are impressive in the level of detail I can get even on my old 3080, and they are a technical accomplishment they should be proud of (even when pathing bugs and it sends your framerate to zero).

The rest of the game feels like a series of disparate and unfinished features.  I think this game is an example of the danger of scope creek, and they needed to cut the scope so they can focus on the core game to make a more complete holistic game. It's a collection of barely connected features that are mostly pointless to engage with, including the core questline. Blacksmithing, diplomacy, relationships, tournements, trading, etc, are functionally not very worth engaging with. Battle AI is pretty good, but campaign map AI is very bad. You can end up stuck whacking moles because your own kingdom seems to like sending underpowered armies and getting your entire military killed off, and then going ahead and declaring wars on new kingdoms anyway. You basically have to do it all yourself until your enemies are so thoroughly defeated that your AI can finally help a little with castle capture. 

It's shame they couldn't keep feature creep in check it could have been great.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that key information on how to perform certain actions is omitted from standard gameplay explanations and appears only on loading screens.

citations.review_text:
I have played every Mount & Blade since the first, and Warband will always be the GOAT.

Bannerlord is an incredible let down:

Some of the key information only appears on loading screens, like how to follow a party.
The game does absolutely NOTHING to teach the player about chambering attacks.
Stealth segments are rudimentary at best. No way to stab an enemy sitting on the ground, from behind. Asinine

Dear Taleworlds,

Please start hiring and PAYING people to polish the game(s). If you will not improve the quality of your games then at least let someone else do it. There is not much to celebrate in this installment compared to Fire & Sword. Sure, the graphics are improved, but the game mechanics and level of polish are relatively low compared to previous titles. 

Neither making the game prettier nor setpieces can save the overall game quality from nosediving when there is a jarring lack of polish across every part of the game, in mechanics and appearance.  

At a minimum, let me be able to backstab bandits sitting on the ground.

A degrade from previous title.
Bones of gameplay such as UI, hitboxes, combat responsiveness and fighting/running animations are worse than in Warband. Multiplayer killfeed log doesn't even show what weapon was used. Any campaign module mod from workshop/moddb i tried lead to crashes despite perfect installation.
You can have 10 warband mods instead and still it takes less storage space than this modern garbage in vanilla alone, that only has better environment textures.

claims.claim: AI allies make counterintuitive decisions such as sieging distant locations without food while losing wars.

citations.review_text:
Every lord in this game got goofy ahh decision making.
We are losing the war badly.
Cool. Let’s siege a random castle 900 miles away with no food.

Enemy nobles escape prison like it’s a part time job.
Khuzaits moving around the map like they got creative mode enabled.

I genuinely started tweaking whenever some random lord with 11 troops raided my village, ran away for 3 days, then came back and did it again.
Still somehow one of the most addicting games I’ve played.
Recommended.
